text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: Alert triggered for service=runtime-gpu-prod, severity=critical. Trigger reason: 50% increase in 5xx across west-* regions. PagerDuty incident: https://pd.example/INC12345

harper: paging chain fired but it looks like it went to eng-sre instead of eng-runtime. anyone seeing the same?

liang: saw it. eng-sre got the pages. oncall schedule mapping for runtime-gpu-prod points to the legacy eng-sre policy. this should be eng-runtime-policy.

devon: acked to stop noise (I thought it was our infra flake). sorry — I should not have acked without verifying.

ana: @devon np, we need to confirm impact first. harper can you confirm which customers hit 5xx?

harper: quick check: hits concentrated on west-1 and west-2. unusual spike for requests proxied through dedicated pools. customer-facing errors: increased 502/504 for batch-embedding endpoints. I have a few logs attached.

harper: ```
2026-03-14T18:41:02Z runtime-gpu-prod loadbalancer: upstream failed: connection reset
2026-03-14T18:41:05Z runtime-worker-12: kv cache miss + long tail latency
```

liang: looks like we ran out of available VMs in dedicated pool and fallback routing tried a model variant that timed out. But PD service mapping error means the wrong responder group got paged.

sre-oncall: I can take this if needed, but I'm not the runtime SME. who owns the dedicated pools?

ana: @sre-oncall you can coordinate with @harper/@liang. harper, can we mitigate with a routing tweak to send requests to fallback read-only pool to reduce errors?

harper: trying a quick config flip to prefer cached replicas. running:
```bash
# toggle routing policy to prefer cached-replicas
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/routing/override -d '{"service":"runtime-gpu-prod","policy":"prefer-cached","ttl":600}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT'
```

harper: applied override. watching metrics.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Routing override applied by harper. Incident tagged: routing-override.

devon: I just removed my ack and re-notified the runtime oncall via PD. The correct eng-runtime policy has been contacted. apologies for the earlier ack.

liang: good. can we also fix the PD service mapping? looks like the integration was pointing runtime-gpu-prod -> eng-sre-policy due to a config drift after last schedule rotation.

harper: opening quick PR to update mapping and add a guard: new check will compare PD service->slack channel mapping against the oncall schedule API.

harper: PR: https://git.internal/routing/PR/892 (hotfix)

ana: customer impact notes for postmortem: roughly 8% p50 latency increase, 30-40% error spike for 10m window; affected customers: three enterprise customers on dedicated pools, some read-only fallbacks. add severity: customer-visible outage (partial).

liang: escalation policy action item: add a rule that disallows manual schedule overrides without a secondary approver. and add runbook step to confirm PD mapping after any schedule change.

sre-oncall: for handoff, I'll stay on until runtime oncall picks up. @harper please update status page when we confirm stabilization.

harper: metrics look stable now after override. error rate down to baseline in west-*. keeping watch for 20m. will post update to status when we hit 30m stable. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: :memo: Incident assigned to postmortem: owners=harper, liang; severity=partial-customer-outage; timeline-start=1812345000

devon: follow-up tasks: 1) PD service mapping hotfix (harper) 2) schedule audit (oncall rotation owner) 3) add automated PD->oncall verification test (liang) 4) retro and customer comms (na).

harper: noted. I'll draft the customer impact blurb after stabilization.
